GABRIEL H M: "VACUUM ARC DISCHARGES USED TO DEPOSIT HARD WEAR RESISTANT COATINGS ONTO TOOLS" PROCEEDINGS OF THE INTERNATIONAL SYMPOSIUM ON DISCHARGES AND ELECTRICAL INSULATION IN VACUUM,US,NEW YORK, IEEE, vol. SYMP. 15, 1992, pages 643-645, XP000342798 ISBN: 3-8007-1856-1
PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN vol. 1996, no. 03, 29 March 1996 (1996-03-29) & JP 07 310171 A (KOBE STEEL LTD), 28 November 1995 (1995-11-28)

abstract.p: Wear resistant coating deposited on a substrate, containing B and N elements, is created at least by two layers of which the first layer has internal stress exceeding 1 GPa, thickness exceeding 0.1 mu m and consists predominantly of Ti and N elements, the second layer being created predominantly by Ti, N, B elements, with at least 5 % contents of B and thickness at least 0.5 mu m. The process of creating a wear resistant coating on a substrate by depositing is performed by vapor plating by low voltage arc in a reaction atmosphere by way of a physical method (PVD) and/or chemical method from a gaseous phase under the presence of plasma (PACVD), the ionisation of plasma for depositing by PACVD being effected by low voltage arc. The apparatus for preparing wear resistant layers using the method of low voltage arc with cathode (2, 2a, 2b) being arranged in a coating chamber. The axes of cathode (2, 2a, 2b) is substantially vertical, a source of magnetic field being available for the cathode (2, 2a, 2b). The source of magnetic field is preferably at least one electromagnetic coil (11, 12, 11a, 11B, 12a, 12b).

Ce revêtement résistant à l'usure, déposé sur un substrat, contenant les éléments B et N, est constitué d'au moins deux couches, la première présentant une contrainte interne supérieure à 1 Gpa, une épaisseur supérieure à 0,1 mu m et étant principalement constituée des éléments Ti et de N tandis que la seconde couche est principalement constituée des éléments Ti, N et B, avec une teneur en B d'au moins 5 % et a une épaisseur d'au moins 0,5 mu m. Le procédé de production de ce revêtement résistant à l'usure sur un substrat met en oeuvre un placage en phase vapeur réalisé au moyen d'un arc à faible tension dans une atmosphère réactionnelle et ce, par le biais d'une technique physique (dépôt physique en phase vapeur) et/ou d'une technique chimique à partir d'une phase gazeuse en présence de plasma (dépôt chimique en phase vapeur à l'aide de plasma). L'ionisation du plasma aux fins du dépôt chimique en phase vapeur à l'aide de plasma se fait grâce à un arc à faible tension. L'appareil permettant de produire des couches résistant à l'usure fait intervenir la technique de l'arc à faible tension avec cathode (2, 2a, 2b) placée dans une chambre d'enduction. Les axes de la cathode (2, 2a, 2b) sont sensiblement verticaux. La cathode (2, 2a, 2b) dispose d'une source de champ magnétique, laquelle source est, de préférence, au moins une bobine électromagnétique (11, 12, 11a, 11B, 12a, 12b).

description.p: WEAR RESISTANT COATING

Field of invention This invention relates to an wear resistant coating deposited on a substrate containing elements B and N. It also relates to the process of producing an wear resistant coating on a substrate by deposition and apparatus for the preparation of wear resistant layers by low voltage arc process, the cathode being located in a coating chamber, especially for carrying out this process.
Background of invention

Coatings are known that represent hard wear resistant layers applied on an object and made of other material, such as metal, usually on a cutting tool. Manufacturing such object with subsequent application of coating on its cutting areas can considerably improve the utility features of the tool, especially its service life, and also a broader scope of applications is enabled wherein the tool would not be operable without such coatings, and further higher cutting speed etc. Various known coatings are produced, such as TiN, MoN, WN, TiC, A1203, Si3N4, B4C, ZrN, HfN, A1N and their combinations in form of multilayer coatings, such as TiN + A1203, or in form of multicomponent coatings and their solid solutions, such as TiAIN, TiCN. The layers made thereof, however, have limited hardness and chemical as well as thermal stability, which hampers their utilisation for heavy duty tools.

Superhard layers on the basis of Ti-B-N are known that are prepared by application methods called Physical Vapor Deposition (further only PVD). In case the PVD technology apparatus uses gas as the source of boron, such as B3N3H6, BC13 etc., a combined technology is already involved, PVD/PACVD, and boron and its compounds are deposited on the surface of the evaporating or sputtering PVD electrode intended for evaporation or pulverisation. On the
one hand, this results in reducing the speed of coating, on the other hand the coating parameters may change uncontrollably; the so-called intoxication of the cathode can occur.

Technologies of depositing wear resistant TiAlSiN layers are also known where metallic electrodes made separately of titanium and aluminium for Ti and Al vapor deposition are used, and either a metallic Si electrode or a gaseous component, such as SiH4, are used as Si source. Technologies are known using TiAISi alloy as source of material. These technologies can not be efficiently applied if a low voltage arc is used for vapor depositing, the TiAISi alloy, or possibly pure Si, being unsuitable for evaporation in a low voltage arc, due to substantial increase of the number and size of macro particles. In case gaseous Si, such as SiH4, is used as source, the process becomes instable and problems concerning the maintenance of stable stoichiometry of the coating are seen to occur. Also processes and apparatuses are known for depositing protective layers onto objects by way of the above mentioned physical method, namely Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD), or by a chemical method, namely Chemical Vapor Deposition (further only CVD), or by a chemical method from gaseous phase in the presence of plasma, namely Plasma Assisted Chemical Vapor Deposition (further only PACVD).

In case of the PACVD method a process is generally used wherein the layer grows in a glow discharge, one electrode of which being located directly on the objects to be coated, i.e. the charge to be coated. The glow discharge burns directly in the gas mixture that is the source of coating material. The disadvantage of this method resides in poor regularity of coating growth on the charge to be coated.

One of the solutions of the PVD method has been described and illustrated in the Czech patent specification No. 276840. According to this method the object to be coated is arranged in a vacuum coating chamber. The
evaporation of the coating material located in the centre of the chamber is achieved by low voltage electric arc, the evaporating material being one of the electrodes, and namely the cathode. The objects to be coated are located close to the walls of the coating chamber, and negative voltage is applied to them. This results in accelerating positively charged ions directed to the objects to be coated. Modifying this negative voltage during the coating process can partially regulate the temperature of these objects. The evaporating electrode can be positioned in a magnetic field that accelerates the cathode spot and reduces the number of macro particles that are generated during the application of this technology.

The disadvantages of the previous embodiment reside in particular in that there is no way of controlling the regularity of the cathode spot motion over the surface of the whole cathode. That is why such solution does not allow multicomponent coatings with defined components ratio to be deposited in a controlled way.

The aim of the present invention is the creation of a protective coating consisting of various layers, a process of producing the same and an apparatus for performing this process, doing away, to greatest possible extent, with the drawbacks of the present art and allowing to establish layers consisting of various layers and using different technologies, in one single process. Summary of the invention

The substance of the protective coating according to the invention resides in that it is created by at least two layers of which the first has internal stress exceeding 1 GPa, thickness more than 0.1 μm and consists, predominantly, of Ti and N elements, the second layer consisting, predominantly, of Ti, N, B elements, with at least 5 % B and thickness at least 0.5 μ .

It is essential, for improving the adhesion of the second layer of the coating on the first layer, to create a transition layer between the first and
second layer, the concentration in said layer continuously changing in direction from the fist layer to the second layer, and namely the Ti concentration decreases, while the concentration of B or N is increasing.
Regarding the characteristics of the layer it is substantial that the concentration changes at least in three steps or continuously, the minimum thickness of the transition layer being 50 nm.

The substance of the process of creating an wear resistant coating on a substrate by depositing consists in that the deposition is achieved by evaporation caused by low voltage arc in a reaction atmosphere by a physical method (PVD) and/or by a chemical method from a gaseous phase under the presence of plasma (PACVD), the ionisation of plasma for depositing by way of PACVD being ensured by low voltage arc.

Concerning the regularity of a coating on a substrate, the contribution is seen in that at least a part of the coating material is deposited on the substrate after evaporation from the cathode of the low voltage arc, a controlled source of magnetic field surrounding the cathode.

Regarding the quality of coating it is significant that the fomentation takes place by evaporating from a cathode of which at least one part consists predominantly of an AlSi alloy with atom content of Si between 3 and 30 %, the second part of the cathode containing at least some of the elements of transitory metals.

The substance of the apparatus for the preparation of wear resistant layers by method of low voltage arc with a cathode located in a coating chamber resides in that the axis of the cathode is basically vertical, a source of magnetic field being applied to the cathode.

Regarding the controllability of the magnetic field it is important that the source of magnetic field is at least one electromagnetic coil, preferably two electromagnetic coils being provided for each cathode, said coils being coaxial with the cathode and connected with a control device.
Concerning reliable burning of the low voltage arc it is a contribution that an anode of the low voltage arc is provided for each electromagnetic coil at its outer side or, possibly, the coat of the electromagnetic coils operates as the anode of the low voltage arc. The substantial benefit of the coating according to the present invention is the improvement of its physical characteristics.

The substantial benefit of the process according to the present invention resides in that it allows to produce hard and superhard coatings using the combined PVD/PACVD method, while substantially suppressing the intoxication of the electrode intended for evaporating material by the PVD method, such as in case of Ti-B-N coatings where a gaseous component, such as B3N3H5, is being applied as boron source.

Another advantage of the invention consists in that it allows the preparation of multicomponent coatings with continuously adjustable proportions of separate components of the coating directly in the course of the process, such as TiAlN layers with continuously adjustable Ti:Al ratio.
One of the advantages of the invention consists in that it allows layers with high B and N contents with good adhesion to be prepared.
The invention is beneficial also in that it allows TiAlSiN layers to be prepared by PVD method by way of low voltage arc technology.

Another preferable embodiment of the invention resides in that if a conductive component is created by PACVD technology, the described apparatus allows also the exclusive application of the PACVD process, such as in the TiCl +N2+H2 mixture for producing a TiN layer. The benefit of the PACVD process in an apparatus according to the present invention resides in the fact that the ionisation field of reaction components is separated from the field of depositing the actual layer on the substrate. This enables the elimination of one of the basic drawbacks of the PACVD technology, namely
the irregularity of coating growth. The ionisation in this case is not brought about by glow discharge, but by the aid of low voltage arc. Brief description of the drawings

Embodiments of the invention are illustrated in drawings where Fig. 1 shows a diagrammatical section of the coating chamber with the apparatus according to the invention, Fig. 2 shows another embodiment of a part of the coating apparatus, and Fig. 3 an apparatus according to the invention having two cathodes. Examples of embodiment of the invention The coating chamber 1 accommodates, in its centre or its axis, an evaporating electrode of coating material, serving as cathode 2 of the low voltage arc having approximately the form of a cylinder that can be tapered at both ends. As a rule, the axis of cathode 2 is vertical. Both ends of the tapered parts of cathode 2 can be provided with pole shoes 3. The centre of the evaporating electrode, i.e. cathode 2, is created by the actual functional part 5. This functional part 5 can consist of a plurality of zones, each of them having different material composition. In a preferable embodiment the first zone 6 is of titanium and the second zone 7 of aluminium. Inlets 10 of reaction gases mouth into the coating chamber 1. Cathode 2 is provided with a source of controlled magnetic field, which can be embodied, e.g., so as to consist of a hollow upper electromagnetic coil 11 and a hollow bottom electromagnetic coil 12 that are symmetrically arranged at both sides of cathode 2. Accordingly, cathode 2 is accommodated in a magnetic field created by both coils 11 and 12. The internal diameter of the coat of both electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 exceeds the external diameter of the evaporating electrode, i.e. cathode 2. The bodies of the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 are accommodated at the upper wall 11 and the bottom wall 9 of the coating chamber 1, respectively. Both electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 have substantially cylindrical form and their winding ends at the beginning of
the cylindrical part of the evaporating electrode, i.e. cathode 2. The described arrangement of electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 is a preferable embodiment.

They can be arranged in a different way, e.g. cathode 2 can be accommodated inside the electromagnetic coil as its core. The coat of the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 can create the anode of a low voltage arc (Fig. 2) and can be galvanically connected with the coating chamber 1, or it can be galvanicaly separated from the coating chamber 1, such as by insulation 33 (Fig. 1).

Embodiments according to Figs. 1 and 3 are provided with adjacent electrodes at the outer sides of each of the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12, this electrode according to the example of embodiment being anode 13 of the low voltage arc. Anode 13, the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12, including their coats, and cathode 2 are arranged substantially in one axis. Both electromagnetic coils 11 and 12, anode 13 as well as cathode 2 are cooled, cooling liquid being supplied into their coats or into the cavity 14 (Fig. 2) in the evaporating electrode/cathode 2 through the ducts 15a and drained through outlets 15b.

The objects to be coated/substrate 16 are accommodated in the current way in the coating chamber 1 close to its lateral wall 17 (Figs. 1 and 3). The coating chamber 1 is provided with evacuation outlet 19 for the connection of a not illustrated vacuum device and is also electrically earthed by earthing 30
(Fig. 1). The evacuation outlet 19 serves also as outlet for inert gases.

Adjacent to cathode 2 the ignition electrode 20 is arranged, in the example of embodiment it is located at the upper part of cathode 2. Prior to starting the apparatus chamber 1 of the coating apparatus should be sufficiently evacuated and then filled with reaction gas, such as nitrogen or inert gas, such as argon.

For starting the operation of the apparatus negative coating voltage from the source 32 (Fig. 1) shall be applied to the substrate 16, i.e. on the
subject to be coated, and the source 31 of low voltage arc shall be applied between cathode 2 and anode 13. With the aid of ignition electrode 20 the low voltage arc is ignited in the current way. The burning area 21 (Figs. 1 and 2) is created by a ring surrounding cathode 2 and extending between both anodes 13 (Fig. 1) or between coats 25 and 26 of the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 (Fig. 2), respectively. The negative bias of substrate 16 attracts positively charged particles evaporated from cathode 2 and ionised by the arc. Accordingly, a layer created by material of cathode 2 and the reaction gas is deposited on the surface of substrate 16. It can be summed up that at least a part of the coating material is deposited on the substrate after having been evaporated from cathode 2 of the low voltage arc, a controlled magnetic field surrounding cathode 2.

The current of the arc tends to range between 100 and 300 A, the voltage of the arc between 20 and 30 V, the current of positively ionised particles of the evaporated cathode deposited upon the substrate 16 is usually 4 - 20 A.

Also a not illustrated electrical source is connected to both electromagnetic coils 11 and 12, allowing them to generate a controlled electromagnetic field, as illustrated by line of force 24 in Figs. 1 and 2. Changing the electromagnetic field, i.e. controlling the current in electromagnetic coils 11 and 12, can serve to control the motion of the cathode spot over the surface of the functional part 5 of cathode 2. For this purpose the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 are connected with a not illustrated control device. For preparing a TiAlSiN layer one part of cathode 2 consists of Ti and the other part of Al-Si alloy containing Si within the range of 3-30 at %; the reaction atmosphere is usually created by nitrogen under the pressure of 0.1 to 0.3 Pa. By controlling the current in the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 the motion of the cathode spot over both zones 6 and 7 of cathode 2 can be
controlled, which allows to adjust the stoichiometry of the deposited layer arbitrarily during the process. It can be concluded, accordingly, the vapor plating to be carried out by evaporation from cathode 2, of which at least one part consists predominantly of Al-Si alloy with atom contents Si in the range of 3 - 30 %. This method allows to create TiAlSiN layers with various Ti.AISi ratio or, e.g., multilayers consisting of thin layers with various Ti: AlSi ratio. The second part of cathode 2 contains at least some of the elements of transitory metals, Ti being preferable.

Intensifying the magnetic field by increased current flow through the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 results in stronger ionisation of gases in the region 21 of arc burning, and at the same time the voltage of the arc rises. If introducing reaction gas suitable for the preparation of PACVD technology layers, such as TiCl4 , CH4, B3N3H6, SiH4 etc. for the preparation of TiN, C, BN, Si3N etc into this area, the gas molecules become intensely ionised in this zone and accelerated towards the substrate 16 having negative voltage bias and, consequently, the layer growing on substrate 16 can be prepared partially by the PVD method, i.e. through evaporation of the material from the cathode of the low voltage arc, and partially by PACVD method, and namely thanks to the ionisation of the gaseous reaction components of the respective PACVD technologies in the burning area of low voltage arc. Accordingly, this is a combined PVD-PACVD method. Consequently, the depositing takes place through vapor plating by low voltage arc in a reaction atmosphere by way of a physical method (PVD) and/or by a chemical method from a gaseous phase under the presence of plasma (PACVD), the ionisation of plasma for the deposition by way of PACVD being effected by low voltage arc.

Changing the intensity of the magnetic field can be used for continuous adjustment of the relative shares of the growing layers generated by contributions of the PVD and PACVD technologies. One of the advantages of this system resides in that the evaporated cathode 2 can be relatively small,
which results in high evaporating intensity of the coating material from a unit surface of cathode 2. This can substantially eliminate the intoxication of the cathode.

The described way can be used, by way of example, for preparing composite layers TiN-Si3N4 where a part of TiN is created by the PVD method through evaporating Ti from cathode 2 in nitrogen atmosphere, a part of Si3N4 being created by ionisation of SiH4 in the burning area of low voltage arc; by reacting with nitrogen, that is part of the reaction atmosphere, the Si3N component is formed. The proportion TiN:Si3N4 is usually in the range between 3: 1 and 10: 1.

Similarly also a layer consisting of Ti, B and N elements can be prepared, and further Ti-B-N, while the Ti:B:N ratio can, but need not be stoichiometric, and the source of boron can be, e.g., T3N3H6. If, in a PACVD process e.g. the mentioned B3N3H6 compound is used as reaction gas, or another compound containing boron, such as B2H6, BC13, Bι0H14 etc., and as material for cathode 2 titanium is used, then this combined PVD-PACVD method allows to prepare a Ti-B-N layer in nitrogen atmosphere. The HV (hardness according to Vickers) of such layer can exceed 50 GPa.

The above process can be used for creating coatings with at least two layers having a layer of Ti-B-N of at least 0.5 μm thickness that is deposited on a bottom layer created by a layer with internal stress exceeding 1 GPa and thickness over 0.1 μm, e.g. consisting of titanium nitride TiN. The bottom layer with internal pressure consists, predominantly, of Ti and N elements, such as TiN. This first layer can be deposited directly on the substrate, the Ti and N ratio being preferably stoichiometric, but neither are indispensable. The second Ti-B-N layer can, but need not be the last layer of the coating. The first layer can be located directly on substrate 16, but it can be also positioned on one layer or more layers deposited on the substrate by known procedures. Accordingly, it can be concluded that the coating is created by at least two
layers of which the first layer has internal stress exceeding 1 GPa and thickness exceeding 0.1 μm, the second layer consisting predominantly of Ti, N, B elements, with at least 5 % of B content and at least 0.5 μm thickness.

Another preferable embodiment of the coating according to the invention consists in that between the layer with internal stress, such as TiN, and the Ti-B-N layer, as described above, a transitory layer is created wherein the concentration of the elements gradually varies from the layer with internal stress towards the Ti-B-N layer. The concentration can change in steps, however, at least in three steps. The Ti concentration is decreasing and the B, and possibly also N, concentrations increase, and namely continuously or step- wise, while these steps do not exceed 10 atom % Ti. The minimum thickness of this transitory layer is 50 nm.
Exemplary characteristics for depositing a superhard and wear-resistant Ti-B-N layer according to the invention: Voltage on substrate: 100 to 300 V

Current density on substrate: approx. 0.05 A per square cm Current in the arc: 100 to 150 A Voltage of the arc: 26 to 30 V Flow B3N3H6: 20 seem per minute Flow N2: 35 seem per minute Pressure: 0.2 to 0.6 Pa Cathode applied: titanium
Current density of arc at the Ti cathode: 1 to 2 A per square cm Note: 1 seem stands for standard cubic centimetre corresponding to the amount of gas in one cubic centimetre under normal pressure.
In all above examples of embodiment Ti can be replaced by one of the transitory metals, such as molybdenum or tungsten.

Another embodiment of an apparatus according to the invention (Fig. 2) differs from the above described apparatus in that the function of the above
mentioned anode 13 of the low voltage arc is performed by coats 25 and 16 of the electromagnetic coils 11 and 12 and, consequently, positive voltage of the source 31 of the low voltage arc is applied on these coats 25 and 26. For improving the burning stability of the low voltage arc a screening 27 is arranged inside the electromagnetic coils, e.g., in form of cylinders. Such screening is beneficial, but not indispensable, and the apparatus according to the invention can be embodied without screening.

For improving the capacity of coating chamber 1 two evaporating electrodes can be accommodated in this chamber, and namely cathodes 2a and 2b (Fig. 3) and, possibly, also a plurality of cathodes 2a and 2b. In proportion to that also a corresponding number of electromagnetic coils, igniting electrodes, etc. should be used. The difference as compared with the embodiment according to Fig. 1 consists especially in that both electromagnetic coils 11a and l ib of the upper cathode 2a are attached to the upper wall 1 of the coating chamber 1 by a not illustrated bracket, whereas both electromagnetic coils 12a and 12b of the bottom cathode 2b are attached to the bottom wall 9 of coating chamber 1 by a not illustrated bracket. A preferable connection between the coats of electromagnetic coils 11a and l ib of the upper cathode 2a is ensured by interconnection 28 and between the coats of electromagnetic coils 12a and 12b of the bottom cathode 2b by another interconnection 29. Such interconnection 28 or 29 can be preferably embodied as a number of pipes, such as three pipes serving also for cooling the internal coils l ib and 12a, while being useful for supplying current to these electromagnetic coils 11a, l ib, 12a, and 12b. Industrial applicability

Coatings according to the present invention are intended especially for creating hard and superhard surface layers on machining tools, e.g. cutting tools. It is also beneficial to provide such coatings on tools for milling, turning and boring as well as on tools for metal product finishing operations, such as
honing and, possibly, also other tools requiring high resistance against abrasion and wear.

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS

1. Wear resistant coating deposited on a substrate, containing B and N elements, characterised in that it is created by at least two layers of which the first layer has internal stress exceeding 1 GPa, thickness exceeding 0.1 μm and consists predominantly of Ti and N elements, the second layer being created predominantly with Ti, N, B elements and having at least 5 % B and at least 0.5 μm thickness.

2. Wear resistant coating according to claim 1 characterised in that between the first and the second layer a transitory layer is created wherein the concentration continuously changes in direction from the first layer to the second layer, the Ti concentration decreasing and the B or N concentration increasing.
3. Wear resistant coating according to claim 2 characterised in that the concentration changes at least in three steps.
4. Wear resistant coating according to claim 2 characterised in that the concentration changes continuously.

5. Wear resistant coating according to any of the claims 2 to 4 characterised in that the minimum thickness of the transitory layer is 50 nm. 6. Process of creating an wear resistant coating on a substrate by depositing, such as for creating an wear resistant coating according to one of the above claims, characterised in that the deposition is performed by vapor plating effected by low voltage arc in a reaction atmosphere, by physical method (PVD) and/or a chemical method from gaseous phase under the presence of plasma (PACVD), the ionisation of plasma for depositing by way of

PACVD being effected by low voltage arc. 7. Process according to claim 6 characterised in that at least a part of the coating material is deposited on the substrate after evaporation from the
cathode of the low voltage arc, a controlled magnetic field being created at the cathode.

8. Process according to claim 7 characterised in that the vapor plating is effected by evaporation from a cathode, of which at least a part is created by Al-Si alloy with up to 30 atom % of Si3 contents.
9. Process according to claim 8 characterised in that the second part of the cathode contains at least some of the transitory metal elements.

10. Apparatus for the preparation of wear resistant layers by method of low voltage arc with the cathode arranged in a coating chamber, in particular for performing the process according to some of the claims 6 to 9, characterised in that the axis of the cathode (2, 2a, 2b) is substantially vertical, a source of magnetic field being adjacent to the cathode (2, 2a, 2b).
11. Apparatus according to claim 10 characterised in that at least one electromagnetic coil (11, 12, 11a, l ib, 12a. 12b) is the source of magnetic field.

12. Apparatus according to claim 10 or 11 characterised in that for each cathode (2, 2a. 2b) two electromagnetic coils are provided (11, 12, 11a. 1 lb, 12a, 12b) that are co-axial with the cathode (2, 2a, 2b). 13. Apparatus according to claim 11 or 12 characterised in that each electromagnetic coil (11, 12, 11a, l ib. 12a, 12b) has an adjacent anode (13) of the low voltage arc at its external side.
14. Apparatus according to claim 10 or 11 characterised in that the coat (25, 25) of the electromagnetic coils (11, 12, 11a, l ib, 12a, 12b) represents the anode of the low voltage arc.

15. Apparatus according to claims 10 to 13 characterised in that the electromagnetic coils (11, 12, 11a, l ib, 12a, 12b) are connected with a control device.
